schemaNote: Single source of truth for CLI flag regression coverage, consumed by ClaudeCodeCliFlagMatrixTest (parse-contract layer) and, later, by the process-level startup smoke. Every `expect` value below was measured from a real parse rather than derived by hand: it is the exact set of CliLaunchRequest fields that change relative to an argument-free parse. An empty diff therefore means the flag is not wired in, and an extra key means it leaked into another axis.

statusNote.ALIGNED: Behaviour matches 2.1.197 (or is a deliberate Java-only addition).
statusNote.KNOWN_DIVERGENCE: Asserts current Java behaviour on purpose, so that either fixing or further breaking it shows up as a failure instead of passing silently.
statusNote.MISSING: Present in 2.1.197, absent from the Java CLI. Ledger only — no executable case.

197 binds -v to --version. Java binds it to --verbose and puts version on -V. `claude -v` therefore does entirely different things on the two builds.
197 is `-d, --debug [filter]` and consumes the category filter. Java declares a boolean, so the filter silently becomes the initial prompt instead.

This table asserts parsing only. The post-parse identifier chain 197 applies to the value — a .jsonl transcript first (absolute and case-sensitive interactively, any case-insensitive suffix under --print), else a UUID, else an exact case-insensitive custom-title search across same-repo worktrees — is covered by CliResumeTargetResolverTest, and its per-mode reporting by CliSessionRestoreCoordinatorTest.

197 coerces the optional value with `value => value || true`, so a bare -r requests the interactive picker. Picocli yields "" for a bare arity-0..1 option; null still means the flag was absent, which is the distinction CliSessionRestoreCoordinator routes on.
197's `value || true` makes an explicitly empty value indistinguishable from a bare -r; both request the picker.
The long form takes the same optional value, so `--resume` alone also requests the picker.
Java-only flag; 197 only reads the theme from settings.
Comma form works via Picocli split.
Variadic like 197's `<directories...>`: one occurrence takes every following non-option token.
Greediness is inherited from 197: a variadic option consumes the trailing positional prompt too. Pinned so the shared shape with --tools/--mcp-config stays visible.

Deliberately absent from the launch snapshot: routed through AgentTeamsEnabled.setCliFlag() in call(). An empty diff is the correct contract here. Not a 197 commander option either — it only appears as a string in the bundle.
Parenthesised rules stay one token; CliToolSelection.parseToolList splits later.
Comma splitting is deliberately downstream in CliToolSelection.parseToolList, which also honours parentheses. The parse layer keeps the raw token.

Explicit empty list means "disable all tools" and must stay distinguishable from the null of an omitted flag. Picocli keeps the empty token, so the observed value is [""] rather than []; CliToolSelection.parseToolList drops it downstream via StringUtils.isEmpty, leaving an empty selection.
